title: Tension pneumothorax
claims: Normal coronal view: trachea midline, mediastinum central, both lungs inflated, right hemidiaphragm slightly higher than left.
Tension pneumothorax: air enters the pleural space through a one-way valve; intrapleural pressure rises.
Tension pneumothorax: the ipsilateral lung collapses; the mediastinum and trachea shift away; the hemidiaphragm flattens; the contralateral lung is compressed.
Kinking of the great veins reduces venous return, causing obstructive shock (hypotension, JVD, tachycardia).
Exam: absent breath sounds and hyperresonance on the affected side. Clinical diagnosis: do not wait for imaging.
Immediate needle decompression (classically 2nd intercostal space, midclavicular line; ATLS 10th ed. for adults: 4th/5th intercostal space just anterior to the midaxillary line), then chest tube.
